summary: Transient identity handshake and MFA handover policy question for international hire onboarding
description:
Issue summary:

We're evaluating a short-lived onboarding pattern for hires joining from abroad where shipping hardware takes 2+ weeks. HR and Security want a documented and auditable flow that lets new hires start work with minimal risk. This ticket asks for clarity on acceptable temporary identity/service-account patterns, MFA handover rules, and device-binding expectations.

Background:
- New hire (software engineer) based in APAC has start date before hardware arrival.
- Current options considered: 1) loaner company laptop shipped locally, 2) temporary shadow account with limited privileges, 3) contractor-style bridge account.
- Security wants MFA to be enforced, but hardware (company phone) will arrive later than start date.

Impact:
- If we don't define a standard: teams create ad-hoc exceptions, inconsistent audit trails, and potential over-privilege windows.
- Teams reported delays in ramp time and onboarding blockers for early-start hires.

Request:
- Confirm policy for (a) issuing timebound shadow accounts, (b) acceptable MFA alternatives until company device available, and (c) required steps to convert temporary identity to full employee account and revoke temporary creds.

Desired output:
- A concise policy bullet list and a recommended runbook for Support/IT to follow per-hire.
steps_to_reproduce: Not a bug; reproduction steps are the real-world onboarding scenario: 1) Offer accepted with start date < hardware ETA; 2) HR requests access so hire can start; 3) Team requests IAM access; 4) Temporary credential issued via ad-hoc process. We need to formalize.
investigation_notes: Spoke with HR Ops (K. Lin) on 2026-03-09 — common case ~3 hires/month in last 6 months for APAC/EU where device arrives after start date.

Security (J. Rosen) raised two constraints: (1) no shared credentials, (2) MFA must be enforced but can be TOTP app or FIDO2; hardware phone not strictly required if user has a personal device enrolled under a temporary policy.
IT ticket patterns show repeated creation of temporary service accounts named temp/onboard/{name} without unified expiry metadata — increases audit burden.
Existing referenced ticket INT-224518 documents a prior 'bridge-account' flow for contractors — we should avoid reusing contractor privileges for employees.
comments: Elena Garcia (Reporter) 2026-03-10: Flagging because hiring manager needs guidance before next week's start date.
Maya Thompson (Assignee) 2026-03-11: Can SRE/IT provide a recommended template for a timebound account and default scopes? I'll coordinate with Security and HR Ops.

James Rosen (Security) 2026-03-11: Preference is timebound user-scoped accounts with strict least-privilege roles; allow TOTP-on-personal-device as a temporary MFA, but require enrollment into company SSO device registry within 7 days of hardware arrival.
Karen Lin (HR Ops) 2026-03-12: We can accept a 14-day exception window for full provisioning if we get a standard sign-off checklist to use per hire.
proposed_workaround: Until policy is finalized: issue a named, timebound 'temp/onboard/{firstname_lastname}' account scoped to developer-readonly + developer-sandbox (no prod access). Enroll TOTP on the user's personal device with explicit waiver signed by manager and HR. Add expiry metadata tag and schedule automated revocation 14 days after creation unless converted. Ensure all steps recorded in IT ticket before account activation.
next_steps: 1) Security to approve minimal role set and acceptable MFA methods (owner: J. Rosen) by 2026-03-16. 2) HR Ops to confirm manager sign-off checklist (owner: K. Lin) by 2026-03-16. 3) IT to produce an automation template for creating timebound accounts with expiry tags (owner: Maya Thompson) by 2026-03-18.
resolution: Pending — awaiting Security/HR sign-off and automation template. Temporary workaround accepted by HR for this hire per comment but must be replaced with formal runbook.
notes: Audit requirements: any temporary account must be logged in our central audit index and tagged with 'temp_onboard' and manager name. Converting temp account to full employee account should require rebind of MFA to company-managed device when available.
